title: To Be: I am, You are, He/She/It is
description: Learn the foundation of English sentences: the verb 'to be' in positive, negative, and question forms.
objectives: Introduce yourself and others using 'am', 'is', and 'are'
Form positive and negative statements with personal pronouns
Ask and answer simple questions about identity and professions

vocabularyList.definition: A person who is studying at a school, college, or university.
A person who teaches, especially in a school.
Feeling or showing pleasure or contentment.
A person whom one knows and with whom one has a bond of mutual affection.

sections.title: Understanding the Verb 'To Be'
sections.content:
The verb **to be** is the most important verb in English. It links a subject (who or what) to information about that subject (who they are, how they feel, or where they are).

In the present tense, 'to be' has three forms: **am**, **is**, and **are**.

callouts.title: Contractions in Daily Speech
callouts.text: Native speakers almost always use contractions like **I'm**, **you're**, and **she's** in casual conversation.

callouts.title: Common Mistake
callouts.text: Never say 'I is' or 'They is'. Match the pronoun: I am, You/We/They are, He/She/It is.

timeline.title: State of Being (Right Now)
timeline.explanation: The simple present of 'to be' expresses a current permanent or temporary state of fact.

examples.english: I am a student from Lahore.
examples.urdu: میں لاہور سے ایک طالب علم ہوں۔
examples.audioText: I am a student from Lahore.

examples.urdu: وہ ہماری انگریزی کی استانی ہیں۔

examples.english: They are not tired; they are ready.
examples.urdu: وہ تھکے ہوئے نہیں ہیں؛ وہ تیار ہیں۔
examples.audioText: They are not tired; they are ready.

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.english: Hello! I am Sara. Are you the new student?
dialogue.urdu: ہیلو! میں سارہ ہوں۔ کیا آپ نئے طالب علم ہیں؟
dialogue.audioText: Hello! I am Sara. Are you the new student?

dialogue.speaker: Ali
dialogue.english: Yes, I am! My name is Ali. It is nice to meet you.
dialogue.urdu: جی ہاں، میں ہوں! میرا نام علی ہے۔ آپ سے مل کر خوشی ہوئی۔
dialogue.audioText: Yes, I am! My name is Ali. It is nice to meet you.

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.english: Nice to meet you too! Mr. David is our teacher. He is very kind.
dialogue.urdu: آپ سے بھی مل کر خوشی ہوئی! مسٹر ڈیوڈ ہمارے استاد ہیں۔ وہ بہت مہربان ہیں۔
dialogue.audioText: Nice to meet you too! Mr. David is our teacher. He is very kind.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence: 'Sarah and I _____ excited about the new course.'
exercises.explanation: 'Sarah and I' represents 'we' (first person plural), so the correct verb form is 'are'.
exercises.urduExplanation: 'Sarah and I' جمع فاعل (ہم / We) ہے، اس لیے فعل 'are' استعمال ہوگا۔

exercises.prompt: She _____ (not be) at home right now; she is at work.
exercises.explanation: With third-person singular 'she', the negative present form of 'to be' is 'is not' or contracted 'isn't'.
exercises.urduExplanation: ضمیر 'she' کے ساتھ منفی شکل 'is not' یا 'isn't' بنتی ہے۔

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order to form a polite question:
exercises.explanation: Questions with the verb 'to be' invert the subject and verb: 'Are' (verb) + 'you' (subject) + 'ready' (adjective) + 'for the exam'?
exercises.urduExplanation: سوالیہ جملے میں فعل 'Are' فاعل 'you' سے پہلے آتا ہے۔

exercises.prompt: Match each subject pronoun with its matching form of 'to be':
exercises.explanation: I matches 'am'; third-person singular matches 'is'; plural and second-person pronouns match 'are'.
exercises.urduExplanation: I کے ساتھ am، واحد غائب کے ساتھ is، اور جمع/تم کے ساتھ are آتا ہے۔

sections.title: اردو بولنے والوں کے لیے رہنمائی
sections.urduText: انگریزی زبان میں جملہ بنانے کے لیے فعل (Verb) کا ہونا لازمی ہے۔ اردو میں ہم کہتے ہیں: 'میں طالب علم ہوں'۔ انگریزی میں 'ہوں' کے لیے 'am' استعمال ہوتا ہے: 'I am a student'۔ اردو کی طرح انگریزی میں فعل کو چھوڑا نہیں جا سکتا۔ کبھی بھی 'I student' نہ کہیں، بلکہ ہمیشہ 'I am a student' کہیں۔

sections.title: Lesson Summary
summaryPoints: The verb 'to be' has three present forms: am (I), is (he/she/it), are (you/we/they).
Contractions (I'm, she's, they're) are standard in conversational English.
To make negatives, add 'not' after the verb: 'He is not' or 'He isn't'.
To make questions, invert the subject and verb: 'Are you ready?'
